methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: AI Ready Roanoke represents deliberate regional capacity-building outside NoVA, but success depends on whether this produces deep local expertise or shallow adoption of externally-developed tools—a pivot point between distributed depth and continued concentration.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Local backlash canceling four NoVA data centers signals infrastructure limits in the state's AI hub, potentially constraining even concentrated development while offering no redistribution benefit to other regions—a lose-lose outcome that aligns with neither depth nor distribution.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: A statewide AI cybersecurity plan suggests platform-level protective tools deployed broadly across agencies—enabling shallow but distributed adoption where users consume AI-powered security without building deep defensive capabilities internally.

signals.title: Military spouse uses AI to help veterans navigate VA benefits - DC Military
signals.signal_reading: A military spouse creating an AI tool for veterans' benefits navigation exemplifies grassroots, purpose-driven AI development outside traditional tech centers—precisely the peer-to-peer capability building that characterizes distributed depth over platform dependency.

signals.title: Virginia Tech Science Festival returns with immersive AI exhibits - WDBJ7
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech's immersive AI exhibits signal educational infrastructure for building regional AI literacy beyond NoVA, creating conditions for distributed capability development if hands-on engagement translates to local implementation rather than talent export to metro hubs.
